source.title_on_document: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing

supplement.where: The paper mentions no supplementary material. Appendices A-E (prompts, quiz, design problems, pilot study, demographics) are inside this PDF, pp. 17-25. Footnote 1 (p. 1) links an interactive demo: https://joongishin.github.io/problemReframing_llm/
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the appendices in this PDF. No table of arm means, SDs, or test statistics for novelty and usefulness exists anywhere in the document.

paper_design_summary: Designers recruited on Prolific and CloudResearch (456 recruited, 280 analyzed after exclusions) were randomly assigned to reframe one of three design problems either without an LLM (MANUAL) or with GPT-4o in one of three ways: DIRECT (button-generated frames), STRUCTURED (button-driven Dorst nine-step chain), or FREE-FORM (own ChatGPT account). Each participant wrote two problem frames and picked the best one; 15 high-quiz-score participants then rated those 280 best frames for novelty and usefulness. Agency, ownership, perceived helpfulness (CSI), and effort (NASA-TLX) were self-reported.

studies.label: Main online experiment (problem reframing, four conditions)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Reframing approach (MANUAL, DIRECT, STRUCTURED, FREE-FORM) and one of three design problems (aging, misbehavior, preference conflict)
assignment.quote: Our study followed a between-subjects design with four levels: (MANUAL, DIRECT, FREE-FORM, and STRUCTURED). Participants were assigned to these conditions in line with balanced Latin square randomization.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1; also p. 5, Section 4 ('We randomly assigned participants to one of the conditions') and p. 7, Section 4.5

arms.name: MANUAL
arms.description: Baseline: designers reframe the problem without an LLM.

arms.name: DIRECT
arms.description: Designers press a 'Reframe' button that prompts GPT-4o with fixed prompts to (re)generate alternative problem frames, and build on or submit them.

arms.name: STRUCTURED
arms.description: Button-driven GPT-4o prompt chain that follows Dorst's nine-step reframing process and shows intermediate content (apparent problems, stakeholders, themes) plus final frames.

arms.name: FREE-FORM
arms.description: Designers converse freely with the default ChatGPT (GPT-4o) through their own account and submit the conversation log.

participants.exclusions: 456 recruited and randomly assigned (Figure 4). 176 removed after assignment: those who failed attention checks, submitted frames in incorrect format, or spent less than 10 minutes on the reframing task, plus people assigned to an LLM approach who did not use the LLM. Per-reason and per-arm exclusion counts are not reported. The non-use exclusion applies only to LLM arms, so exclusion may differ by arm. Arm sizes analyzed are unbalanced (62, 72, 88, 58). A chi-squared test finds the expert/novice split balanced across arms (chi2(3, N = 280) = 0.70, p = 0.87; p. 11).
participants.who: Crowdsourced individuals with design experience (product, UI/UX, graphic, game design, architecture, fashion); 76% had more than three years of design experience; 145 women, 128 men, 7 other; paid 16 euros, plus a 5-euro bonus for the top 10% of frames.
participants.quote: We also removed people who were assigned to LLM-based approaches but did not use LLMs. In the end, we had 280 participants (145 identifying as women, 128 as men, and seven as "other"
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2 and Figure 4; arm counts p. 9, Figure 8 (table); demographics p. 25, Table 10

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT-4o (August 2024); FREE-FORM used the default ChatGPT version with participants' own accounts
ai_tool.how_used: Mixed across arms. DIRECT supplies LLM-generated problem frames on a button press (ideas supplied). STRUCTURED supplies LLM-generated intermediate content and frames through a fixed nine-step prompt chain (ideas supplied, guided). FREE-FORM is open chat with ChatGPT. Participants could submit LLM frames directly or build on them, and had to write an explanation for each frame.

task.description: Problem reframing: given a design problem description, write two alternative problem frames ('If the problem of {initial problem} is approached as if {alternative perspective}, then the direction of solutions could be {potential solutions}') judged most novel and useful, then pick the best one in the post-survey.
task.duration: Mean time to create two frames: 23.25 min (SD 14.73) MANUAL, 21.82 (11.95) DIRECT, 28.35 (18.00) STRUCTURED, 20.78 (9.34) FREE-FORM (p. 8, Section 5); paid for 'their hour of effort' (p. 6).

outcomes.name: Novelty of the problem frame (expert rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 15 'expert' raters drawn from the study's own participants who answered 3+ of 5 quiz items correctly (Table 11, p. 25); each reviewed 36 frames randomly sampled across 4 approaches x 3 problems x 3 frames (p. 6). Questionnaire adapted from Doshi and Hauser [21]; plotted on a 1-9 axis (Figure 5). How ratings are aggregated per frame and how many raters scored each frame are not stated. Tests: Mann-Whitney U (MANUAL vs LLM-ALL), Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's test, Bonferroni (four approaches).

contrasts.reported: "there were no statistically significant differences for either, between the MANUAL and the LLM-ALL group but also among all the individual approaches (all p > 0.05)"; box plots only (Figure 5). No means, SDs, or test statistics printed.
Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc (Bonferroni) across the four approaches: "all p > 0.05"; Figure 5 box plots by arm.
Among the individual approaches, "all p > 0.05" (Dunn's test, Bonferroni).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Experts (3+ quiz items correct) within LLM-ALL
contrasts.control_arm: Novices (0-2 quiz items correct) within LLM-ALL
contrasts.reported: Not an AI contrast (heterogeneity by participant expertise, H4). "significant differences in the novelty of the LLM-conditioned frames (Z = 2.70, p = 0.01): the experts generated 12.54% more novel frames than the novices"; FREE-FORM gap 20.84%, Z = 2.31, p = 0.06. No starred expert-novice gap in MANUAL in Figure 10.

outcomes.name: Usefulness of the problem frame (expert rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 15 participant-experts and same procedure as S1-O1; plotted on a 1-9 axis (Figure 5). Tests: Mann-Whitney U (MANUAL vs LLM-ALL), Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's test, Bonferroni.

contrasts.reported: "there were no statistically significant differences for either, between the MANUAL and the LLM-ALL group but also among all the individual approaches (all p > 0.05)"; box plots only (Figure 5).
Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc (Bonferroni): "all p > 0.05"; Figure 5 box plots by arm.
Not an AI contrast. "As for the usefulness of frames, no statistically significant differences emerged across the approaches (all p > 0.05)."

studies.label: Pilot study (feasibility of the three design problems)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Design problem and approach (three participants per problem x approach cell)
assignment.quote: we recruited 36 people (17 self-identifying as women and 19 as men) from design-related industries and randomly assigned three participants to each design problem and approach

participants.exclusions: Not stated. Per-arm counts of 9 follow from 3 per problem x 3 problems; the paper states 3 per cell and 12 per problem.
participants.who: People from design-related industries, same platforms as main study
participants.quote: Using the same procedure and platforms as for the main study, we recruited 36 people

task.description: Same problem-reframing task; used only to check that the problems could be reframed.

company_involvement.description: Funded by the Research Council of Finland, Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence, European Research Council, and Aalto University departments. GPT-4o was used as a tool; no company involvement stated.

eligibility.reason: S1 randomly assigns individuals (balanced Latin square, p. 5) to no LLM or one of three GPT-4o approaches; 280 people analyzed (456 randomized), at least 58 per arm; novelty and usefulness of each participant's best frame are rated by 15 expert raters (pp. 6, 8-9). Caveats: 176 post-assignment exclusions, including LLM-arm participants who did not use the LLM (possible differential attrition); raters are themselves study participants; only box plots and 'all p > 0.05' are printed, with no arm means or SDs. The pilot (S2, n = 36) is below 50 and reports no arm contrast.

one_line_finding: Among 280 crowdsourced designers randomized to reframe a problem without an LLM or with GPT-4o in three ways, expert-rated novelty and usefulness of the best frame did not differ between MANUAL and LLM-ALL or among approaches (all p > 0.05; pp. 8-9, Figure 5).
open_questions: No arm means, SDs, or test statistics for novelty and usefulness are printed; extraction would need data from the authors or digitizing the Figure 5 box plots (medians and quartiles only).
Per-arm randomized counts and per-arm exclusion counts are not reported; the exclusion of LLM-arm non-users happens only in AI arms.
The number of raters per frame and how ratings were combined are not stated (15 raters x 36 frames = 540 ratings for 280 frames implies about two ratings per frame, but the paper does not say so).
Whether problem reframing counts as idea_generation or 'other' task type.
notes: Outcomes not listed because they are self-reported, not scored on the output: perceived agency and ownership (Figure 6, p. 8; all p > 0.05), Creativity Support Index for LLM arms (DIRECT 64.28, SD 18.90; STRUCTURED 64.85, SD 20.00; FREE-FORM 61.01, SD 17.19; p. 10), and NASA-TLX effort (Figure 7, p. 9). Time to create frames is reported by arm (p. 8) but is not a creativity outcome. Expert-novice agency gap in LLM-ALL Z = 2.05, p = 0.04; STRUCTURED Z = 2.29, p = 0.02 (p. 12). Each participant wrote two frames; only the self-selected best frame (280 frames) was rated, so the output count equals the person count. Power analysis: G*Power required 220 and 280 participants for medium effects at 95% power (p. 8, Section 5.1). The search-record note 'N=280 with no unit stated' is confirmed as 280 people (p. 6).
